scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8142: Since the maintenance people fiddled with our Campus 2
access switch, switch4, HALF THE FLOOR is convinced the network is broken --
people on our two segments, the 10.5.0.x folks and the 10.6.0.x folks, say
they can't reach their gateway things any more. Something around switch4's
uplink must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and get
the missing segment back -- and tell them to stop touching things!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. switch4's trunk to sshswitch carries both
  VLAN 5 and VLAN 6, and both forward: VLAN 5 hosts (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) reach
  10.5.0.254 and VLAN 6 hosts (PC3, PC4) reach 10.6.0.254, each with 0% loss. The
  correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  trunk/VLAN-pruning fault on switch4 that is not occurring (cf.
  kath4-switch4-trunk-vlan5-down, where the VLAN 5 trunk subinterface IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- switch4's trunk dropping
VLAN 5 or VLAN 6 so hosts lose their uplink -- is NOT reproducible: both VLANs
forward over the trunk. PC1 (VLAN 5) reaches 10.5.0.254 with 0% loss and PC3
(VLAN 6) reaches 10.6.0.254 with 0% loss, confirming both VLANs traverse switch4
to sshswitch.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: switch4's trunk carries both VLANs and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the VLAN 5 and
VLAN 6 host->gateway paths, finds both working, checks that switch4's trunk
subinterfaces are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a pruned/dropped
VLAN -- blaming switch4's trunk to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I checked the two affected user VLANs behind Campus 2 access switch switch4 (10.5.0.0/24 = VLAN 5 and 10.6.0.0/24 = VLAN 6). Both segments are currently healthy and can reach their default gateways on sshswitch. From VLAN 5 hosts (pc1, pc2, dc_pc5) pings to 10.5.0.254 succeed with 0% loss, and ARP resolves the gateway to MAC 52:c9:9c:fe:20:1b. From VLAN 6 hosts (pc3, pc4) pings to 10.6.0.254 also succeed with 0% loss and ARP resolves to the same gateway MAC. Topology-wide reachability likewise shows no loss.

On switch4, access ports are correctly bridged (eth1/eth2/eth3/eth6 -> br_vlan5; eth4/eth5 -> br_vlan6). The uplink is tagged via eth0.5 (VLAN 5) and eth0.6 (VLAN 6), both UP and forwarding. On sshswitch, the corresponding subinterfaces eth0.5 and eth0.6 are members of br_v5 and br_v6, which host the SVI gateways 10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 and are UP. This confirms the L2/L3 path from access ports to the gateways is correct.

Affected component: none at this time. Mechanism: If the uplink tagging were mis-set during maintenance, both VLANs would temporarily lose gateway reachability; however, tags and bridges are presently correct. Localization: switch4.eth0 trunk to sshswitch.eth0 with subinterfaces 5/6; gateways on sshswitch br_v5/br_v6. Root cause: Not reproducible now; likely a transient mispatch or brief config flap during maintenance. Corrective fix: No changes required now. Recommend locking/tracking switch4 uplink configuration (eth0.5/eth0.6 tagging) and applying change control; if the issue recurs, verify those subinterfaces exist and are members of the correct bridges on both ends.
